糾.meaning: In a silent library, the librarian taps a <part>tuning fork</part> to shush the room, and its hum catches a loose <part>thread</part> on a reader's scarf. The thread spins round the two prongs, tighter and tighter, until scarf and fork are braided into one wild <kanji>twist</kanji>.
糾.on: The reader pokes the knot free with a pool <sound>cue</sound> borrowed from the games room.
糾.kun: Then the librarian checks the scarf for damage and finds only a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>du</sound>ck feather.

賭.meaning: On a rainy pier, <part>someone</part> pushes their only <part>shellfish</part> into the middle of the card table and whispers, 'All in.' The crab across the table slides in one of its own claws. Both stare at their cards, sweating: the most nervous <kanji>gamble</kanji> on the coast.
賭.on: They play on the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, so whoever loses has the longest fall.
賭.kun: Only the crab stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, clicking its last claw on the table.

尼.meaning: A woman in a long black habit climbs the steep hill behind her convent with nothing but a <part>spoon</part>. She digs a tiny hole at the top and plants a <part>flag</part> that reads 'Quiet, please'. Every goat on the hill falls silent for the <kanji>nun</kanji>.
尼.on: When the wind tears the flag, she mends it with a <sound>nee</sound>dle, humming softly.
尼.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasps, as a lla<sound>ma</sound> strolls up and starts chewing the flag.

唆.meaning: High above a fairground crowd, a <part>stilt walker</part> dangles a shiny candy apple on a string. Her painted <part>mouth</part> whispers, 'Come up and take a bite.' Grown-ups start dragging ladders over: she knows exactly how to <kanji>tempt</kanji>.
唆.on: The next night she dangles a silver <sound>sa</sound>rdine instead, and every cat in town follows her.
唆.kun: One cat on a <sound>so</sound>fa and one in a <sound>so</sound>ggy hat say '<sound>No</sound>t me,' then climb after her, <sound>ca</sound>lm as kings.

帽.meaning: A bald gardener knows the noon sun is a <part>risk</part>, so he soaks a <part>towel</part> in the well and wears it folded on his head. By lunch the whole village copies him, and the shop sells out of towels. It's the town's favourite <kanji>cap</kanji>.
帽.on: He wears it all day while rolling a <sound>bou</sound>lder up to his vegetable patch.
帽.kun: His neighbour adds a yu<sound>zu</sound> peel and a pump<sound>kin</sound> stalk on top for style: a hood.

窯.meaning: A potter stacks clay bowls in a <part>hole</part> dug into the hillside, over a bed of <part>hot coals</part>, and seals it up. A curious <part>sheep</part> climbs on top for the warmth and dozes all night. By morning it has the toastiest, curliest wool in the land, fresh off the <kanji>kiln</kanji>.
窯.on: The potter fires a little clay <sound>yo</sound>-yo for the sheep, still warm on its string.
窯.kun: <sound>Ca</sound>lm as a cloud, the sheep lets grand<sound>ma</sound> pull the hot bowls out from under it.

貼.meaning: At her seaside booth, a <part>fortune telling</part> lady presses a <part>shellfish</part> to her ear to hear the future. It clamps onto her cheek and won't let go. She reads palms all summer with a limpet on her face, because some things just <kanji>stick</kanji>.
貼.on: She tells customers it's her new <sound>cho</sound>ker, just worn a little high.
貼.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs a customer with a <sound>ru</sound>by ring, and sticks one on her own cheek.

薦.meaning: A lost hiker finds a mountain <part>shed</part> where a hermit roasts chestnuts over <part>hot coals</part> and lays fresh <part>grass</part> on the floor for a bed. He sleeps like a log. Back home, he tells every friend he meets to go: he can't <kanji>recommend</kanji> it enough.
薦.on: Even the <sound>sen</sound>try at the border post takes his advice and goes on holiday.
薦.kun: The hermit keeps serving <sound>su</sound>shi, then more <sound>su</sound>shi, urging every guest to have another.

餓.meaning: Stranded on a raft with crates of <part>food</part> cooked by his rival, a famous chef lets his <part>ego</part> win: 'I'd rather eat my own shoe.' Three days later the crates are still sealed, his pride is fat, and he is about to <kanji>starve</kanji>.
餓.on: A seagull drops a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic on the raft, and he eats it raw, since that counts as his own recipe.
餓.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' he says, swallowing the last clove before the seagull can ask for a bite.

升.meaning: A bored rice seller tips her wooden measuring box on its side as a tiny <part>goal</part> and flicks grains into it. Each good shot she marks with a chalk <part>slash</part>. When the box is full to the brim, she knows she has exactly <kanji>1.8 liter</kanji>s of rice.
升.on: Shoppers stop to cheer, and her stall becomes the best <sound>show</sound> in the market.
升.kun: Then she scoops the rice out with a <sound>mu</sound>g into a pot for <sound>su</sound>shi.

萎.meaning: A garden <part>committee</part> meets on the lawn to decide how to water the <part>grass</part>. They vote, re-vote, form a smaller committee and break for biscuits. By the time they agree, every blade has curled up brown. Long meetings make lawns <kanji>wither</kanji>.
萎.on: Only the <sound>ee</sound>l in the pond stays fresh: it never went to a meeting.
萎.kun: '<sound>She</sound> said to water it!' cries the chair, pointing at an <sound>o</sound>ctopus sprinkler nobody switched on.

斬.meaning: An ice sculptor carves a giant <part>car</part> with a proud ice driver at the wheel. The mayor says it's too tall for the parade tunnel, so she swings an <part>axe</part> and the driver's frozen head slides off down the street. The crowd gasps at the cleanest <kanji>beheading</kanji> in ice history.
斬.on: The ice head skids into the lap of a <sound>zon</sound>ked guard asleep in a deck chair.
斬.kun: She slices the leftover ice into <sound>ki</sound>wi slush for the crowd: to cut.

塚.meaning: A <part>pig</part> drags its <part>blanket</part> into the yard and noses <part>soil</part> over it, scoop after scoop, until it can climb up and see over the fence. It spends every afternoon up there, admiring the view from the top of its own little <kanji>hillock</kanji>.
塚.on: It wears a daisy <sound>cho</sound>ker like the queen of the hill.
塚.kun: A gust of dust makes it sneeze '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', but the pig stays <sound>ca</sound>lm on its throne.

穂.meaning: A busy ant asks the tallest <part>grain</part> stalk for a <part>favor</part>: 'Bend down, please.' The stalk bows low, heavy at the top, and the ant climbs onto the plump, bristly head and carries off one seed. That's the generous <kanji>ear of grain</kanji>.
穂.on: The ant trades the seed for a wrapped <sound>swee</sound>t at the anthill shop.
穂.kun: It carries the sweet home across a <sound>ho</sound>t stone path, hopping.

伺.meaning: A famous film <part>director</part> visits his old drama teacher's tiny flat. He hangs his fancy coat on her humble <part>coat hook</part> and bows low, holding a bunch of daisies. No cameras today: he has come to <kanji>pay respects</kanji>.
伺.on: She greets him holding the cardboard <sound>shie</sound>ld from his very first school play.
伺.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' he says, knocking it over, but stays <sound>ca</sound>lm and mends it with a bit of chewing <sound>gu</sound>m.

芳.meaning: Far out at sea, a homesick sailor weaves fresh-cut <part>grass</part> into his <part>sail</part>. Every gust sprays the smell of a summer meadow across the deck. Fish rise to the surface and line up to sniff the <kanji>perfume</kanji>.
芳.on: When the sail dries out, he sprays it with a <sound>ho</sound>se and the scent blooms again.
芳.kun: He tucks a <sound>carn</sound>ation behind his ear and dabs his lips with lip <sound>ba</sound>lm that smells of hay.

廉.meaning: An old man runs his shop from a garden <part>shed</part> and does everything <part>concurrently</part>: he sells, wraps, sweeps and chats all at once. He's so busy he forgets the prices and lets everything go for a penny. The queue stretches round the block for the <kanji>bargain</kanji>.
廉.on: A <sound>wren</sound> hops in and buys a whole bag of seeds for one shiny button.

鐘.meaning: A <part>juvenile</part> fox finds a lump of <part>gold</part> in a stream and taps it with a stick. Bong! It rings so loudly the whole valley wakes up. The fox hangs it from a branch by its den and calls it his <kanji>bell</kanji>.
鐘.on: Every evening he puts on a ringing <sound>show</sound> for the owls.
鐘.kun: The owls stay <sound>ca</sound>lm, nodding along in their <sound>ne</sound>st.

捉.meaning: A clumsy sailor's <part>foot</part> tangles in the rope as the <part>anchor</part> drops, and he's yanked overboard. Underwater he wraps both arms round the anchor and simply refuses to let go, cheeks puffed. No fish has ever seen such a firm <kanji>grasp</kanji>.
捉.on: He bobs back up still hugging it, but missing one <sound>sock</sound>.
捉.kun: The crew haul him up on <sound>to</sound>p of the deck and hand him a hot bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

枢.meaning: A city <part>ward</part> runs out of metal, so its carpenter grows the door hinges instead. She plants a <part>tree</part> beside every front door and trains a bendy branch to curl round the frame. Doors creak open on living wood: every house has a green <kanji>hinge</kanji>.
枢.on: When one door sticks, a <sound>su</sound>perhero swoops down and oils it.
枢.kun: The carpenter checks it from the <sound>to</sound>p with a <sound>bo</sound>ttle of oil, wiping the drips with a <sound>so</sound>ck.

披.meaning: Dragging her <part>anchor</part> across a sandbank, a fisher hooks a buried <part>pelt</part> and hauls it up, sand pouring off. Rolled inside it is a treasure map, laid bare to the sky for the first time in a hundred years. The tide has decided to <kanji>expose</kanji> it.
披.on: She pins the map down with the <sound>hee</sound>l of her boot so the wind can't take it.

堆.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> wants the best view in the park, so it carries <part>soil</part> in its beak, crumb by crumb, all summer long. By autumn its little mound is taller than the park bench. The bird perches proudly on top of earth <kanji>piled high</kanji>.
堆.on: It wears a tiny <sound>tie</sound> for the opening ceremony.
堆.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' it chirps, dropping a yu<sound>zu</sound> seed, a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>ca</sound>lm little snail onto the top.

僕.meaning: At a midnight station, a tired <part>porter</part> hangs fifty coats on one <part>coat hook</part> and stacks fifty suitcases beside it without a wobble. The station master gasps, 'Who did all this?' The porter taps his chest and smiles: '<kanji>Me</kanji>.'
僕.on: His only helper, a <sound>box</sound>er dog, wags at the praise.
僕.kun: '<sound>She</sound> needs a <sound>mo</sound>p,' says the boss, pointing at a cleaner, and off he goes again, then back to make her a <sound>be</sound>d: a servant.

箇.meaning: An explorer leaves a fresh <part>bamboo</part> stalk to <part>harden</part> in the desert sun, then snaps it into neat little tags. On each one she writes a thing in her pack: rope, map, teapot. Now everything she carries has its own tag, one per <kanji>item</kanji>.
箇.on: The last tag goes on a paper kite shaped like a <sound>ca</sound>rp.

貢.meaning: In a sea cave, an old otter sits at his <part>workbench</part> and polishes the finest <part>shellfish</part> shell he can find until it gleams like a pearl. He swims it to the lighthouse keeper who once saved him and leaves it on her step: a <kanji>tribute</kanji>.
貢.on: She thanks him with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, which he eats on his back in the waves.
貢.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>? For me?' she asks, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the sea spray.

塀.meaning: Two neighbours argue over a strip of <part>soil</part> between their gardens. One plants a <part>flag</part> in it; the other drags in old <part>rugby posts</part> and nails planks between them. By sunset a tall line of planks splits the plot in two: a <kanji>fence</kanji>.
塀.on: They stuff the gaps with <sound>hay</sound> so neither can peek at the other's roses.

韻.meaning: Every time the door <part>chime</part> dings, a bored bank <part>employee</part> must greet the customer in verse: 'Welcome, sir, the rain is cold; would you like to save your gold?' The queue claps. Her manager insists every greeting must <kanji>rhyme</kanji>.
韻.on: She writes each one down in purple <sound>in</sound>k for the staff noticeboard.

昭.meaning: From her balcony, an opera singer sends one long high <part>call</part> up at the grey sky. The clouds split, and the <part>sun</part> pops out as if to take a bow, flooding the street with light. Every window in town is <kanji>shining</kanji>.
昭.on: The neighbours cheer from their rooftops at the best <sound>show</sound> of the year.

匿.meaning: When guests arrive, a <part>young</part> puppy leaps into the open sock <part>drawer</part> and pulls a sock over its head. Only its tail pokes out, wagging hard. It is sure it has found the perfect place to <kanji>hide</kanji>.
匿.on: The clock on the dresser goes tick-<sound>tock</sound>, counting how long it lasts.
匿.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm old cat curls up beside it like a <sound>cu</sound>shion and shelters it until <sound>Ma</sound>ma leaves.

宰.meaning: From the <part>roof</part> of her restaurant, the head chef watches the kitchen through a skylight, chewing a raw <part>chili</part> to stay sharp. Too much salt? She drops down a note. Burnt rice? Another note. She doesn't cook; she's there to <kanji>superintend</kanji>.
宰.on: Up there she keeps a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der to cool her mouth after the chili.
